name: ops-mission-control
description: An autonomous ops first responder. Watches your alarms, pages, and monitors; claims what fires; investigates it with real context; and proposes a fix — keeping everything it learns in a local ledger so the second occurrence is faster than the first.
author: kirocrew
highlights: Claims a firing alarm within one heartbeat and investigates before anyone has to look
Knowledge ledger with confidence and trust levels — a repeat failure resolves from what you already know
Live board in the dashboard and as replyable Slack threads, so the channel is the dashboard
Connects AWS CloudWatch, PagerDuty, Datadog, GitHub Issues, or any system that can POST signed JSON — including Alertmanager-shaped bodies, fanned out one incident per alert
Read-only by default — write actions are opt-in per signal pattern, and every one is audited
Rotation-aware: the on-shift automation tier arms and disarms itself

crons.name: dispatch
crons.message: Follow the dispatch SOP at ~/.kiro/crew/skills/ops-mission-control/sops/dispatch.md. Call POST /api/apps/ops-mission-control/dispatch to claim any unclaimed signals; it returns each claimed incident with its ledger matches, operating mode, and a ready-to-use investigation brief. For each claimed incident, create a chat slot whose key is EXACTLY ops-mission-control-<incident_id> (the dashboard incident panel polls that key, so any other key leaves the user watching an empty conversation) titled '<incident_id> - <signal title>', link it to your ops channel so the thread is replyable, and start the investigation from that brief following ~/.kiro/crew/skills/ops-mission-control/sops/investigate.md. Tell the investigator explicitly that Phase 4 is mandatory: it MUST record its diagnosis with POST /api/apps/ops-mission-control/incident/transition (an incident with no recorded diagnosis shows on the board as 'Stopped, no diagnosis', which misreports a finished analysis as a dead end). If the response reports changed=false, produce NO output at all - this job is silent by design.

crons.name: reconcile
crons.message: Follow the reconcile SOP at ~/.kiro/crew/skills/ops-mission-control/sops/reconcile.md. FIRST: GET /api/apps/ops-mission-control/state and if no provider has configured=true, produce NO output and stop - the app is not set up yet, so there is nothing to reconcile and this must cost nothing. Otherwise GET /api/apps/ops-mission-control/signals, then resolve any open incident whose signal is no longer firing (POST /incident/transition), update its Slack thread reaction, and unpin finished work. Cap at 10 incidents per run. If nothing changed, produce NO output.

crons.name: rotation-check
crons.message: Follow the rotation-check SOP at ~/.kiro/crew/skills/ops-mission-control/sops/rotation-check.md. FIRST: GET /api/apps/ops-mission-control/state and if no provider has configured=true, produce NO output and stop - the app is not set up yet, so there is nothing to arm and this must cost nothing. Otherwise POST /api/apps/ops-mission-control/rotation/arm, which resolves the shift and arms or disarms the app's crons itself. You do NOT choose which crons to pause: the route computes the tier map and refuses to pause an always-tier job, so a mistake here cannot strand the instance unable to re-arm. If the response reports an empty changed list, produce NO output.

crons.name: ledger-hygiene
crons.message: Follow the ledger-hygiene SOP at ~/.kiro/crew/skills/ops-mission-control/sops/ledger-hygiene.md. FIRST: GET /api/apps/ops-mission-control/state and if no provider has configured=true, produce NO output and stop - the app is not set up yet, so there is nothing to maintain and this must cost nothing. Otherwise POST /api/apps/ops-mission-control/ledger/hygiene to run the deterministic pass (git pull, dedupe/decay/prune, vector index, retire old closed incidents, git push), then review the remaining entries for contradictions and promote observed->verified where a fix has now worked more than once. Report only if something changed.
